Definition: Text-reported sensitive frequency low endpoint
Note: Sensitive from 1 to 130 kHz; sonic and ultrasonic data use different behavioural criteria. These are not 60-dB SPL hearing-range limits; neither 60-dB endpoint is stated in the paper text. Text only; Fig. 2 was not digitized. Gate: NO_60DB_MAPPING_METHOD_REVIEW. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results

Definition: Text-reported sensitive frequency high endpoint
Note: Sensitive from 1 to 130 kHz; sonic and ultrasonic data use different behavioural criteria. These are not 60-dB SPL hearing-range limits; neither 60-dB endpoint is stated in the paper text. Text only; Fig. 2 was not digitized. Gate: NO_60DB_MAPPING_METHOD_REVIEW. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results

Definition: Hearing threshold at 1 kHz
Note: Sonic range: threshold defined at 75% correct responses by a fitted Gaussian error function; data pooled from five individuals for illustration. Frequency is explicitly 1 kHz. Gate: SONIC_75PCT_ONLY_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination

Definition: Sonic sensitivity plateau low frequency
Note: Plateau at 16 to 22 kHz with threshold about -5 dB SPL; not an exact best-hearing frequency or a 60-dB hearing-range endpoint. Sonic criterion: 75% correct responses; five individuals. Gate: SONIC_75PCT_ONLY_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination

Definition: Sonic sensitivity plateau high frequency
Note: Plateau at 16 to 22 kHz with threshold about -5 dB SPL; not an exact best-hearing frequency or a 60-dB hearing-range endpoint. Sonic criterion: 75% correct responses; five individuals. Gate: SONIC_75PCT_ONLY_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination

Definition: Approximate hearing threshold across 16-22 kHz plateau
Note: The paper says about -5 dB SPL across 16 to 22 kHz. Sonic criterion: 75% correct responses; data pooled from five individuals for illustration. Gate: SONIC_75PCT_ONLY_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination

Definition: Ultrasonic overall threshold range lower value
Note: Text reports overall ultrasonic thresholds of -17 to -3 dB SPL; no exact frequency is assigned to this endpoint. Tested ultrasonic range: 20-130 kHz. Criterion: repeated incorrect responses at the same intensity within a session; means across days weighted by trial counts. Main curve from one animal; a second animal gave similar values. The range is an overall description, not a bound on every threshold; the 50-kHz peak is reported separately. Gate: ULTRASONIC_DISTINCT_CRITERION_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination; PDF p. 3; printed p. 64; Results continuation

Definition: Ultrasonic overall threshold range upper value
Note: Text reports overall ultrasonic thresholds of -17 to -3 dB SPL; no exact frequency is assigned to this endpoint. Tested ultrasonic range: 20-130 kHz. Criterion: repeated incorrect responses at the same intensity within a session; means across days weighted by trial counts. Main curve from one animal; a second animal gave similar values. The range is an overall description, not a bound on every threshold; the 50-kHz peak is reported separately. Gate: ULTRASONIC_DISTINCT_CRITERION_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results and Threshold Determination; PDF p. 3; printed p. 64; Results continuation

Definition: Hearing threshold at 50 kHz minor peak
Note: The paper explicitly reports +2.4 dB SPL at 50 kHz; a minor threshold peak means reduced sensitivity locally. Ultrasonic criterion: repeated incorrect responses at the same intensity within a session; means across days weighted by trial counts. Main curve from one animal; corroboration from a second animal and modified stimulus. Gate: ULTRASONIC_DISTINCT_CRITERION_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF pp. 2-3; printed pp. 63-64; Results; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Threshold Determination

Definition: Frequency above which steep upper audiogram flank is reported
Note: The paper says a steep flank for frequencies above 90 kHz; 90 kHz is a descriptive transition reference, not an exact onset or a hearing-range endpoint at 60 dB SPL. Ultrasonic criterion differs from the sonic 75%-correct criterion. Gate: ULTRASONIC_DISTINCT_CRITERION_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 2; printed p. 63; Results

Definition: Discussion high-sensitivity band low frequency
Note: Discussion describes high hearing sensitivity from 16 kHz to about 100 kHz; this qualitative band has no specified SPL cutoff and must not be treated as a 60-dB hearing range. It summarizes the two differently determined behavioural curves. Gate: QUALITATIVE_BAND_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 5; printed p. 66; Discussion

Definition: Discussion approximate high-sensitivity band high frequency
Note: The high endpoint is explicitly approximate: about 100 kHz. Discussion describes high sensitivity from 16 kHz to about 100 kHz without a specified SPL cutoff; not a 60-dB hearing-range limit. It summarizes the two differently determined behavioural curves. Gate: QUALITATIVE_BAND_NO_60DB_MAPPING. Definitions are method-specific; no central standardized-term changes.
Source Note: Schmidt et al. (1983-1984), Myotis 21-22; PDF p. 5; printed p. 66; Discussion
